content_voiceover: Aplastic anemia is defined by pancytopenia with fatty replacement of the marrow and a near absence of hematopoietic precursors. It's rare, with an incidence of about two per million per year, and has a bimodal age distribution, peaking at fifteen to twenty five years and again at sixty five to sixty nine. Diagnosis requires marrow cellularity below twenty five percent, or below fifty percent if fewer than thirty percent of the remaining cells are hematopoietic. Cytogenetics are usually normal in true aplastic anemia, though you can see six p uniparental disomy in about thirteen percent, and low rates of minus seven or del seven q, plus eight, and minus thirteen q. Severity grading is the classic board question: severe aplastic anemia requires at least two of a reticulocyte count under twenty thousand or under one percent corrected, an absolute neutrophil count under five hundred, and a platelet count under twenty thousand, while very severe aplastic anemia is defined by an ANC under two hundred. The table contrasting hypocellular MDS with aplastic anemia is high yield. Aplastic anemia tends to be bimodal in age, has normal cytogenetics, a PNH clone in twenty to thirty percent of patients, absent blasts, only erythroid dysplasia, and absent or low variant allele frequency somatic mutations without splicing mutations. Hypocellular MDS instead occurs in older patients, has abnormal cytogenetics about half the time, no PNH clone, normal to increased blasts, trilineage or bilineage dysplasia, and canonical MDS mutations including spliceosomal genes. Features specific for MDS over aplastic anemia include dysgranulopoiesis, dysmegakaryopoiesis, and ringed sideroblasts.
keypoints: Severe AA: ≥2 of ANC<500, plt<20k, retic<20k/<1%
PNH clone 20-30% supports AA over primary MDS
MDS-specific clues: dysgranulopoiesis, dysmegakaryopoiesis, ringed sideroblasts
keypoint_voiceover: Know the severity cutoffs cold: severe aplastic anemia needs at least two of an ANC under five hundred, platelets under twenty thousand, or a corrected reticulocyte under one percent, and very severe means the ANC drops below two hundred. Peak incidence is bimodal, young adults and the elderly. A PNH clone favors aplastic anemia over primary hypocellular MDS, while dysgranulopoiesis, dysmegakaryopoiesis, and ringed sideroblasts point you toward MDS instead.
